title: Affine coordinates for coherent completion quotient sections
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, I a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf and P a coherent module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. For an affine open U [def-weil-affine-spectrum], put A=O_X(U), J=I(U) and C=the J-adic completion of P(U). There are A-linear projections p_n:C→(P/I^(n+1)P)(U), for n in the opposite natural-number category. Each p_n is surjective; the p_n are jointly injective and commute with all quotient transitions. On of(x), p_n is the ordinary sheaf quotient of x. If a in A represents eval_n(r) for r in the completed ring, then p_n(r x)=a p_n(x). Every compatible family of quotient sections is p_n(x) for an x in C. These are the canonical quotient-section coordinates.

proof.text: Coherence implies quasi-coherence. The ideal-product comparison computes the positive-power inclusion range as J^(n+1) times P(U); apply the affine cokernel/image theorem to obtain the quotient linear equivalence q_n carrying each class of x to its sheaf quotient.

The quotient transition commutes with q_n by induction on quotient representatives and the defining cokernel-desc equation. Define p_n as q_n composed with AdicCompletion.eval at n+1. Evaluation surjectivity and q_n bijectivity give surjectivity; eval_of gives the ordinary-section formula.

Joint injectivity follows from AdicCompletion.ext at every positive level; the zeroth module quotient is zero. The completed scalar evaluation formula followed by q_n linearity proves the scalar rule.

For a compatible family s, set its n+1 completion coordinate to q_n inverse(s_n), and its zeroth coordinate to zero. The transition equality proves compatibility. The constructed completion element projects to s_n.
